svg.title: SolarEpaperTouch system schematic, revision A
svg.text: IO2 must be high at boot
SDA = MOSI and SCL = SCK: this is an SPI bus, not I²C.
Jumpers A and B open: active-high, momentary output (note 7).
IO0, IO1 and IO3 can wake the ESP32-C3 from deep sleep.
All parts are breakout modules: pin names follow each board's silkscreen. U1 is
drawn from the top, USB-C up, with its pins in physical order.
BT1 (−) goes only to B− on U3. B− is not GND: the system ground is OUT−,
The solar charger output (U2, BATT IN ±) goes to OUT+ / OUT− on U3. U3's
IN+ / IN− and USB-C stay unconnected.
No external diode on PV1: the CN3065 blocks reverse current in the dark
(< 3 µA) and the module already has SS14 diodes. Use a panel with Voc ≤ 6 V.
Turn SW1 off before plugging USB-C into U1: on most SuperMini boards the 5V
pin is tied to USB VBUS.
IO2, IO8 and IO9 are strapping pins. IO2 must be high at boot (R1 makes sure
of it). IO2 and IO8 only carry signals driven by the ESP32. Leave IO9 (BOOT)
TTP223 (U6–U8): jumpers A and B open, so the output is active-high and
momentary. Don't touch the pads at power-up: they calibrate at power-on.
INMP441 (U5): with its clock stopped it still draws 0.8 mA, about 20 times U1 in
deep sleep. Switching it off completely needs a free GPIO.
For low power, remove the power LED on U1 (deep sleep ≈ 43 µA).
